newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CSR wants joint production - paper.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CSR wants joint production - paper.

text.p: Building products group CSR Ltd has said it will approach competitors Boral Ltd and Pioneer International Ltd with a plan to jointly manufacture building products to overcome a damaging price war, The Australian Financial Review reported on Tuesday.
CSR managing director Geoff Kells told the newspaper in an interview the plan would allow the companies to achieve "grander industry restructuring, to be more competitive in export markets."
"I think it's a possibility (that could work) and it's something that we need to talk to the ACCC about, once we have a concrete proposal," Kells said.
The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) is Australia's anti-monopoly regulator.
"A lot of work is going on. We are trying to look at all the possibilities," Kells said.
"It would allow the Australian building and construction materials market to be supplied at lower cost, while retaining a strong competitive market," he said.

Kells said joint venture production arrangements or 50/50 equity investments could be made in the bricks, roof tiles and pre-mix conceret sectors. He said he "certainly expected" Boral and Pioneer to favour the restructuring plan.
"CSR's proposal would involve the industry players sharing factory sites, but separating market and service centre functions," the Australian Financial Review said.

CSR Ltd on Monday prepared shareholders for a second successive fall in annual net profit, blaming its problems on the weak Australian economy and wishing it had more assets invested in the United States.

With major operations in housing, aluminium, sugar, and timber, CSR said net profit in the first six months to September 30 fell 24 percent to A$154.7 million and it forecast lower second half earnings and a likely fall in second half dividend.
CSR shares closed down 10 cents at A$4.18 on Monday.
